title: Applications in healthcare: patient management, hospital efficiency and public health

videos.script: Hospital Jacarandá has 240 beds, and in November they were 85% full. {{average}} That sounds about right. Busy, with a little room. Split it by ward, and intensive care was at 98.5%. Maternity had a third of its beds empty. {{wards}} Nobody is ever admitted to the average. This lesson reads healthcare with the four questions of lesson 17. {{four}} The decisions are where the next patient goes and who can go home. The indicators are beds, stays, waits and returns. The trap is the average that hides the full ward. {{wait}} Then the emergency department, where the median wait and the longest waits tell different stories. {{towns}} Then two towns, where the one that looks sicker turns out to be older. {{privacy}} And the thing that makes health different from every other industry in this course. Almost every row of its data is about a person's body. So the last section is about publishing numbers without publishing people.
